title: Check yourself: Making Claude Code yours: output styles, the status line, keybindings and where each setting lives

questions.stem: A developer selects a built-in style in a settings file with `"outputStyle": "explanatory"`. Replies keep Claude Code's standard wording and no error appears. What is the cause?

options.text: The value must match a name exactly, or the default applies without a message
options.says: The page says "A value that doesn't match a style name exactly, such as `explanatory`, gives you the Default style", with no error.

options.text: The session must be restarted first, because styles are read only at launch
options.says: Ruled out because "Claude uses the new style starting with your next message", and a built-in style needs no restart; only a style file created in a running session does.

options.text: Project files cannot set a style at all, so the value belongs in the user folder
options.says: Ruled out because "A project's own settings files take precedence over that value", so a project file can set a style.

options.text: A hook must apply the choice on each reply, because settings only suggest it to Claude
options.says: Ruled out because a style is applied by Claude Code itself: "Claude Code sends the active style's instructions with every request", and no hook is involved.

questions.stem: A keybindings file sets `ctrl+s` to `null` and `ctrl+c` to a custom action. What results?

options.text: Both keys change as written, and a warning appears on the screen at once
options.says: Ruled out because Claude Code "writes a warning to the debug log", not to the screen, and the reserved key does not change.

options.text: Ctrl+C is rebound as written, and Ctrl+S keeps stashing the prompt as before
options.says: Ruled out because `null` "frees the one key it is written against", so Ctrl+S stops stashing.

options.text: Ctrl+S is freed, and Ctrl+C keeps its default because it is reserved
options.says: The page says `null` "frees the one key it is written against", and that reserved keys cannot be rebound: "These shortcuts cannot be rebound."

options.text: Both keys are freed together, and Ctrl+C then does nothing at all in the chat
options.says: Ruled out because "These shortcuts cannot be rebound", and Ctrl+C is reserved, so it keeps interrupting.

questions.stem: One developer's `~/.claude/settings.json` names an output style, while the repository's `.claude/settings.json` names a different one. Which does the session use?

options.text: The personal choice, because a developer's own file always wins for that person
options.says: Ruled out because "A key at a higher level overrides the same key anywhere below it", and the user level is the lowest of the files.

options.text: The project's choice, because that level outranks the user level
options.says: The page says "Claude Code uses the value from the highest level that sets it", and the shared project settings sit above the user settings.

options.text: Whichever file was saved last, because Claude Code compares modification times
options.says: Ruled out because the documentation gives "their order, highest precedence first", and no file date is involved.

options.text: Neither choice, because a key set at two levels is rejected as a conflict
options.says: Ruled out because "Claude Code uses the value from the highest level that sets it", so two levels are resolved by order and not rejected.
